# Results

<!-- Generated by scripts/make_results.py from results/m2/*.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Research questions:

- **RQ1** How well do linear text classifiers detect each sensitive category at document level, in-domain (dev), under domain shift (test_shift) and out of distribution (test_ood)?
- **RQ2** Do they learn the sensitive content or the document's domain (shortcut learning)?

Task and sets: [TASK.md](TASK.md); data: [DATA.md](DATA.md); background: [theory/01-linear-text-classification.md](theory/01-linear-text-classification.md). The calibration split is not used in this milestone (a guard refuses it).

## Setup

All models were trained on the full train split (79,834 documents). Training every grid took 23.1 minutes in total, within the 45-minute budget that would have triggered a 40,000-document group-aware sample (the decision was taken from a timing probe before any evaluation).

Hyper-parameters were selected on dev only (macro average precision over the six categories). The dev grid, train times (seconds) and the peak memory of each family's own process:

| model | dev macro PR-AUC per C | selected C | grid train s | selected model train s | peak MB | convergence warnings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `word_lr` | C=0.1: 0.9358, C=1: 0.9706, C=10: 0.9793 | 10 (grid edge) | 142 | 81 | 1165 | 0 |
| `char_lr` | C=0.1: 0.9304, C=1: 0.9672, C=10: 0.9782 | 10 (grid edge) | 1165 | 817 | 2827 | 0 |
| `word_svc` | C=0.01: 0.9414, C=0.1: 0.9748, C=1: 0.9810 | 1 (grid edge) | 76 | 50 | 1208 | 0 |
| `domain_lr` | C=0.1: 0.5884, C=1: 0.5883, C=10: 0.5883 | 0.1 (grid edge) | 3 | 1 | 467 | 0 |

`regex_detector` needs no training. `word_svc` scores are margins (default threshold 0); the other trained models output probabilities (default threshold 0.5).

## RQ2: content or domain?

### Domain-only baseline vs text models

Macro PR-AUC; the drop is dev minus the shifted set (positive = worse under shift). Macro averages run over the categories defined in each set (test_ood: 4).

| model | dev | test_shift | test_ood | drop to test_shift | drop to test_ood |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `word_lr` | 0.979 | 0.977 | 0.574 | 0.002 | 0.405 |
| `char_lr` | 0.978 | 0.975 | 0.589 | 0.003 | 0.389 |
| `word_svc` | 0.981 | 0.979 | 0.589 | 0.002 | 0.392 |
| `domain_lr` | 0.588 | 0.364 | 0.369 | 0.225 | 0.219 |
| no-skill (mean prevalence) | 0.324 | 0.361 | 0.369 | n/a | n/a |

- In-domain (dev): `domain_lr` has a lower macro PR-AUC than `word_svc` (0.588 vs 0.981); the no-skill level is 0.324.
- Drop from dev to test_shift: `domain_lr` has a higher drop than `word_svc` (0.225 vs 0.002).
- test_ood has one domain value (`finance`, equal to the training domain `Finance` after case-folding), so the domain-only model gives every test_ood document the same score and its PR-AUC there equals each category's prevalence.

### Top-25 positive features of `word_lr` per category

Annotation rule (fixed before the results; `sensclf.shortcuts`): **field label** if the feature contains a word of a raw dataset label name (generic tokens removed) or a standard abbreviation; otherwise **domain/topic word** if U = MI(F; D) / H(F) ≥ 0.25 on the training documents (F: the feature occurs; D: the domain; U is the share of the feature's occurrence entropy explained by the domain); otherwise **other**.

## Observations

Generated from the tables above; descriptive only.

- dev: the highest macro PR-AUC among the trained models is `word_svc` (0.981).
- test_shift: the highest macro PR-AUC among the trained models is `word_svc` (0.979).
- test_ood: the highest macro PR-AUC among the trained models is `word_svc` (0.589).
- `word_lr on test_shift` has a lower macro PR-AUC than `word_lr on dev` (0.977 vs 0.979).
- `word_lr on test_ood` has a lower macro PR-AUC than `word_lr on dev` (0.574 vs 0.979).
- dev: `word_lr`'s lowest per-category PR-AUC is SPECIAL_CATEGORY (0.961).
- test_shift: `word_lr`'s lowest per-category PR-AUC is CREDENTIALS (0.951).
- test_ood: `word_lr`'s lowest per-category PR-AUC is CREDENTIALS (0.257).
- CONTACT on dev: `regex_detector` has a lower F1 (dev-F1 threshold) than `word_lr` (0.775 vs 0.965).
- FINANCIAL on dev: `regex_detector` has a lower F1 (dev-F1 threshold) than `word_lr` (0.101 vs 0.966).
- Top-25 features of `word_lr` over the six categories: 93 field label, 2 domain/topic word, 55 other.

## Threats to validity

- **Synthetic data.** Both datasets are generated by language-model pipelines. Their templates,
  vocabularies and formatting regularities are easier for n-gram models than real documents,
  so absolute scores say little about real-world performance.
- **Labels come from annotated spans.** A document is positive when the generator annotated a
  span of a mapped raw label. Unannotated mentions make false negatives, and the category
  mapping (docs/TASK.md, Decisions) decides what each category means. A model can be "wrong"
  where the annotation is incomplete.
- **Missing categories in test_ood.** Gretel has no health or GDPR Art. 9 labels, so HEALTH and
  SPECIAL_CATEGORY are undefined there and test_ood macro averages cover fewer categories than
  dev or test_shift; macro values are not comparable across these sets.
- **Prevalence differs between sets.** PR-AUC depends on prevalence (the no-skill level is
  listed next to the domain-only comparison), so part of a PR-AUC change between sets is not
  a change in ranking quality.
- **Selection on dev.** C and the dev-F1 thresholds are chosen on dev, so dev numbers are
  optimistic; test_shift and test_ood are untouched by any choice. The grid is small, and a
  selected C at the edge of its grid (marked in the setup table) may not be the optimum.
- **Uncertainty.** Intervals come from a cluster bootstrap over groups of the evaluation set
  (1000 resamples, seed 0); they do not cover variability from training data or seeds.
- **Domain field.** The shortcut analysis trusts the dataset's `domain` field; the per-domain
  sets are small for some domains, and test_shift domains are mostly unseen by design.
